ideas.name: Chromalux
ideas.niche: AI-driven seasonal color analysis and real-time wardrobe/makeup validation
ideas.problem: Users are highly aware of 'color theory' trends from social media but lack the professional expertise to accurately identify their skin undertones or verify if specific physical products actually align with their personal palette.
ideas.targetUser: Gen Z and Millennial fashion and beauty enthusiasts (ages 18-35) who are active on TikTok/Instagram and want to make more intentional, 'correct' purchasing decisions for clothing and cosmetics.
coreFeatures: AI Skin & Undertone Scanner: Uses the front-facing camera to analyze skin, hair, and eye pigments to assign one of the 12 seasonal archetypes.
Live AR Color Swatching: An augmented reality overlay that allows users to virtually 'try on' different color swatches against their skin in real-time.
Product Match Validator: A tool where users upload a photo of a garment or makeup item to receive a 'Match Score' (0-100%) against their palette.
Curated Seasonal Shop: A personalized feed of product recommendations from partner brands that strictly adhere to the user's specific seasonal profile.
realDependencies: TensorFlow Lite or CoreML for on-device computer vision and color extraction
ARKit (iOS) or ARCore (Android) for real-time color overlays
A robust product database API (e.g., via affiliate networks like Rakuten or Amazon) for shopping integration
Cloud-based image recognition API (e.g., Google Cloud Vision) to identify clothing/makeup items in photos
ideas.emulationStrategy: To simulate the AI Scanner, trigger a 3-second progress bar with 'Analyzing Undertones...' text, then pull a random result from a hardcoded JSON object of the 12 seasonal profiles. For the Product Match Validator, implement a 2-second 'Processing Image...' delay before returning a randomized 'Match Score' and a 'Color Harmony' status (e.g., 'Perfect Match' or 'Clash') from a local mock-database. The AR Swatching will be emulated by displaying static, semi-transparent colored circles over the camera feed that change when the user selects a different palette button.

ideas.name: Pickly
ideas.niche: Gamified collaborative decision-making for micro-social groups.
ideas.problem: Decision fatigue and social friction caused by the mental load of choosing low-stakes activities like dinner, movies, or weekend plans.
ideas.targetUser: Couples (ages 22-40) and small friend groups (3-5 people) who experience 'choice paralysis' during shared leisure time.
coreFeatures: Swipe-to-Select: A fast-paced, Tinder-style interface for filtering food, movies, or activities
Blind Consensus: Prevents social bias by hiding individual votes until everyone has submitted
Chaos Tokens: Limited-use power-ups like 'Veto' or 'Double Vote' to break stalemates
Tie-Breaker Roulette: A randomized spinning wheel for when votes are perfectly split
The 'Maybe Later' Bin: A shared backlog of rejected options to prevent future decision fatigue
realDependencies: Yelp Fusion API for real-time restaurant and venue discovery
TMDB (The Movie Database) API for film and television metadata
Firebase Realtime Database or Supabase for live group synchronization
Google Maps Platform for location-based sorting and distance calculation
ideas.emulationStrategy: Implement a `MockProvider` service that returns static JSON arrays for 'restaurants' and 'movies' to simulate API responses. Every asynchronous call must be wrapped in a Promise with a `setTimeout` ranging from 600ms to 1800ms to mimic network latency. To emulate real-time group voting without a backend, use a local `EventEmitter` to broadcast 'new_vote' events that trigger UI updates across different components. Use `localStorage` to persist user 'Chaos Tokens' and the 'Maybe Later' list, simulating a database session.

ideas.name: Echoic
ideas.niche: Sensory-based, audio-first emotional archiving for the slow-living movement.
ideas.problem: Traditional journaling is high-friction and performative; users struggle to capture the visceral, ephemeral 'vibe' of a moment without the pressure of photography or writing.
ideas.targetUser: Mindfulness-focused adults (ages 25-45), neurodivergent individuals with high sensory awareness, and 'slow living' enthusiasts seeking low-effort mindfulness tools.
coreFeatures: One-Tap Sonic Capture: A single, minimalist button for high-speed 15-second ambient recordings.
Haptic Mood Tagging: Post-recording, users select an emotional state via a quick haptic-feedback icon selector (e.g., Serene, Energetic, Somber).
The Resonance Timeline: A fluid, waveform-based visual scroll that allows users to browse memories through sound rather than text or images.
Atmospheric Playback: A 'Mood Shuffle' mode that plays a sequence of random saved soundscapes to trigger sensory nostalgia.
realDependencies: Web Audio API or native AVFoundation for high-fidelity audio capture
Cloud storage services (AWS S3 or Firebase Storage) for hosting audio files
Relational or NoSQL database (PostgreSQL or Firestore) for metadata and time-series storage
Audio processing library (FFmpeg) for automatic normalization and compression
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local directory of high-quality ambient .wav samples (rain, city, cafe) to bypass real recording. To simulate the cloud, a 'SimulatedUploadService' will use a 2-second Promise delay with a progress bar before resolving with a fake UUID. The timeline will be populated by a static JSON manifest containing timestamps and 'mood' metadata. Visual waveforms will be generated by passing an array of random floats to the UI component to mimic real-time amplitude data.

ideas.name: RuleFlow
ideas.problem: Gameplay momentum loss caused by players needing to pause active sessions to manually search through dense, text-heavy rulebooks for specific edge cases or resolution tables.
ideas.targetUser: Tabletop enthusiasts (Board gamers, TTRPG players, and Wargamers) aged 18-45 who participate in frequent, high-engagement social gaming sessions where maintaining 'flow state' is critical.
coreFeatures: Semantic Rule Search: Natural language search that finds specific mechanics even if the exact phrasing is unknown.
Interactive Decision Trees: Visual, tap-through guides that resolve complex rule conflicts through a series of 'Yes/No' questions.
Crowdsourced Ruling Feed: A community-verified section for 'unwritten' rules and common consensus on disputed edge cases.
OCR Rulebook Scanner: A camera-based tool that uses optical character recognition to instantly link physical book text to digital, searchable summaries.
realDependencies: Cloud Database (e.g., Firebase or PostgreSQL) for rule libraries and community data
OCR Engine (e.g., Google Cloud Vision API) for text extraction
Vector Database (e.g., Pinecone) for semantic/natural language search capabilities
Authentication Provider (e.g., Auth0) for user libraries and profiles
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local JSON file containing a structured 'mock library' of three popular games (e.g., D&D 5e, Gloomhaven, and Warhammer 40k). The OCR feature will be simulated by a 'Simulate Scan' button that triggers a 2.5-second progress bar to mimic processing time before returning a hardcoded text result. The semantic search will be faked using Fuse.js for fuzzy-matching against the local JSON. All 'network' calls will be wrapped in asynchronous functions with randomized delays between 400ms and 1200ms to simulate real-world API latency and loading states.

ideas.name: Endurely
ideas.niche: Crowdsourced product longevity and durability tracking
ideas.problem: Consumers lack transparent data on actual product lifespans, making them vulnerable to planned obsolescence and poor-quality brands that appear high-quality in marketing.
ideas.targetUser: Eco-conscious millennials and budget-focused homeowners (ages 25-45) who prioritize sustainability and value-for-money over brand prestige.
coreFeatures: Smart Scan: Barcode scanning to instantly reveal a product's 'Durability Score' and average reported lifespan.
Lifespan Logging: A streamlined interface for users to record purchase dates, failure dates, and specific failure modes (e.g., mechanical, software, battery).
Brand Reliability Leaderboards: Aggregated rankings of brands and models based on verified user-reported longevity metrics.
Repairability Index: Community-sourced ratings on the ease of finding replacement parts and DIY repair difficulty.
realDependencies: Google Vision API for barcode and product image recognition
UPCItemDB or Amazon Product Advertising API for product metadata enrichment
Firebase Firestore for real-time crowdsourced data storage
Auth0 for secure user authentication and identity management
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a local 'MockRegistry' JSON file containing a subset of 50 pre-defined products mapped to specific hardcoded barcodes. To simulate real-world network conditions, all data fetching functions will be wrapped in an async wrapper that introduces a randomized delay between 800ms and 2200ms. Product metadata will be 'fetched' from this local file rather than an external API. The database will be emulated via an in-memory state object that allows for 'new' logs to be added during the session, providing the illusion of real-time data persistence without a backend.
